gabarito.reason:
org.cry.otp.MD5 is used in only two places, and both are the Mobile-OTP (mOTP) algorithm. mOTP.gen() follows the published spec linked in the class javadoc (motp.sourceforge.net). It derives the 16-hex-char secret as MD5(seed)[0..16]. Each code is MD5(epoch/10s + secret + PIN), truncated to 6 hex chars. Profiles.java:250 uses the same MD5(seed)[0..16] to show the user the secret, which they then enter on the mOTP server. MD5 here is required by an external protocol that the server on the other end checks. The app does not choose it, and nothing here relies on collision resistance: it is a short truncated keyed OTP and a key derivation that both sides must reproduce exactly. If MD5 were replaced with SHA-256 or another digest, every code the app produces would be rejected by mOTP servers. The secret shown in the dialog would no longer match what users have already registered with servers. Every stored mOTP profile (the seed in the DB) would also stop working. So the RVSec finding is a false positive for this app. A PR that changes the digest would break the feature. An issue would only tell the maintainers that the mOTP spec uses MD5, which they already know and cannot change, so nothing useful would be sent. HOTP/TOTP are separate code paths and are not touched by this class.

Second judge: MD5 is part of the supported mOTP protocol, not an independently replaceable digest choice. mOTP.gen derives secret = MD5(seed).asHex().substring(0, 16), then returns the first six hexadecimal characters of MD5(epoch + secret + PIN). Profiles also exposes that same derived secret through View Secret for provisioning. Replacing either hash with SHA-256 would change credentials or generated codes and break existing mOTP verifiers. The report identifies a legacy cryptographic dependency but does not establish a practical authentication bypass. An issue explaining the protocol constraint and discussing coordinated migration is acceptable; taking no action on this generic rule violation is also reasonable. An algorithm-replacement PR is not justified by this finding.
must_not_break: mOTP code generation in mOTP.gen() must stay byte-for-byte compatible with the Mobile-OTP spec: MD5(epoch_10s + MD5(seed)[0..16] + PIN), first 6 hex chars
Codes must still be accepted by existing mOTP servers that users have already enrolled with
The secret shown in the Profiles 'secret' dialog (MD5(seed) first 16 hex chars) must stay the same as the value already registered on servers
Existing stored mOTP profiles (seed, PIN, time zone in the DBAdapter database) must keep producing valid codes after an app update
The HOTP/TOTP code paths, which do not use this class, must not be affected
Existing mOTP profiles: seeds stored in SQLite and copied into SharedPreferences must continue deriving the same first 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters of MD5(seed), including leading zeroes.
Provisioning through Profiles' View Secret must continue showing the same secret already configured on the corresponding verifier.

mOTP generation must preserve the first six lowercase hexadecimal characters of MD5(epoch + secret + PIN), using the existing string encoding, concatenation order, configured timezone offset and ten-second time calculation.
Existing mOTP peers must remain able to validate generated codes. Changing only the client digest, silently converting profiles to HOTP/TOTP, or removing mOTP support would break supported setups.
